Releases of the backbone in the data folder

Source: R/releases.R
WFO.releases.Rd

Lists the releases of the World Flora Online Plant List downloaded by WFO.download() to the per-user data folder of WorldFloraFast, and deletes the ones that are no longer needed (each takes about 1 GB).

Usage

WFO.releases(remove = NULL)

Arguments

remove

Releases to delete, as given in column release of the result (for example "2025-12"). NULL deletes nothing.

Value

A data.frame with one row per release, newest first: release (version), record.id and doi (Zenodo), downloaded (date), size.mb, in.use (TRUE for the release that WFO.read() would use) and file. The data folder is given as attribute folder.

Details

By default, WFO.download() saves each release in its own folder of the per-user data folder of WorldFloraFast, given by tools::R_user_dir() (R_user_dir("WorldFloraFast", "data"), subfolder wfo). This folder is the same in every session and project, and is kept when the package or R are reinstalled. Its location can be changed with the environment variable R_USER_DATA_DIR.

In a new session, WFO.match() (without WFO.data or WFO.file), WFO.read() and WFO.remember() (without WFO.file) use the backbone file remembered by the last call to WFO.download() or WFO.remember(); if that file no longer exists, they use the newest release in the data folder.

Releases downloaded elsewhere with WFO.download(save.dir = ...) are not listed or deleted.

See also

WFO.download(), WFO.read()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
WFO.releases() # releases in the data folder
WFO.releases(remove = "2025-12") # delete an old release
} # }
